steps: Load the bar and stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the bar over the middle of your feet. It should sit about an inch from your shins.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until you can reach down and grab the bar just outside your legs. Grip it with both palms facing you.
Before you lift, get set: pull your chest up, keep your back flat (not rounded), and pull your shoulders back and down. Tighten your stomach as if you were about to be poked there.
Take a breath in, then push the floor away with your feet. Keep the bar close to your body and let it slide up your legs.
As the bar passes your knees, push your hips forward until you're standing tall. Don't lean back at the top.
To lower it, push your hips back first, then bend your knees once the bar passes them. Keep the bar close to your legs until it's back on the floor.
watchFor: Your back is the thing to protect. Keep it flat from your head to your hips the whole time. If it starts to round, the weight is too heavy for now.
Don't yank the bar off the floor. Build tension first, then press the floor away with a steady push.
Start with a light weight, even just the bar, and add slowly over many weeks. If you're new, have someone check your form. Never twist or jerk while holding the weight.
Don't lift with your arms bent. They stay straight and just hold on.

steps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart with the bar on the floor over the middle of your feet.
Push your hips back and bend forward until your upper body is leaning forward at roughly a 45-degree angle. Bend your knees a little.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip (your palms facing your body), just outside your legs, and stand up slightly so the bar lifts off the floor.
Keep your back flat and your head in line with your spine. Let the bar hang with your arms straight.
Pull the bar toward your lower stomach by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Keep your back flat the whole time. If it rounds, the weight is too heavy.
Don't use your body to swing the weight up. If you have to jerk to lift it, lighten it.
Look at a spot on the floor a few feet ahead so your neck stays in line with your back.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar on the floor over the middle of your feet.
Push your hips back and bend forward until your back is nearly flat, parallel to the floor. Bend your knees a bit.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip (your palms facing your body), a little wider than your shoulders.
Tighten your stomach, keep your back flat, and look at the floor slightly ahead of you.
Pull the bar in one quick, strong movement to the bottom of your chest, driving your elbows back.
Lower the bar under control all the way back to the floor, rest for a second, and start the next one from a stop.
watchFor: Your back should stay flat and still. Don't swing your upper body up to help the bar.
Because the bar returns to the floor each time, you can reset and check your form on every rep. Use that to your advantage and start light.
If your lower back starts to round, stop and lower the weight.

steps: Set up the bar so one end is held in place on the floor, in a corner or a small swivel base, and add weight to the free end. Attach a handle if there is one.
Stand over the bar with your feet a little wider than your hips and the bar between your legs.
Push your hips back and bend forward, keeping your back flat, and bend your knees slightly. Grab the handle with both hands.
Lift the weight slightly and let your arms hang straight.
Pull the handle toward your chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause, then lower the weight slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Keep your back flat and don't rock your body to lift the weight.
Look at the floor slightly ahead so your neck stays in line with your back.
Start with a light weight until the movement feels smooth.

steps: Stand next to a flat bench. Place one hand and the same-side knee on the bench, so your back is flat and parallel to the floor.
Put your other foot on the floor, out to the side, for balance. Hold a dumbbell in that hand with your arm hanging straight down.
Keep your back flat and your head in line with your spine, looking at the bench.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body, until your upper arm is just past your back.
Squeeze your back muscle for a moment, then lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish all your reps, then switch sides.
watchFor: Don't twist your body to lift the weight. Your shoulders and hips should stay level.
Keep the movement smooth. Don't jerk the dumbbell up.
Start with a light weight, especially if you feel any strain in your lower back.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet about hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, resting in front of your thighs with your palms facing you.
Soften your knees slightly and keep them at that bend for the whole movement.
Push your hips straight back, as if you're trying to close a door behind you with your buttocks. Let the dumbbells slide down along your legs.
Keep your back flat and your chest lifted. Lower until you feel a strong stretch along the back of your thighs. For most people this is around mid-shin.
Squeeze your buttocks and push your hips forward to stand back up tall.
watchFor: Keep your back flat. If it starts to round, stop lowering. You've gone far enough.
The dumbbells should stay close to your legs. Don't let them drift out in front of you.
The movement comes from your hips going back, not from bending your knees a lot or rounding your back.

steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet hip-width apart. Push your hips back and lean forward until your upper body is almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
Let your arms hang straight down under your chest with your palms facing each other and a small bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to your sides, leading with your elbows, until your arms are about level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the start.
watchFor: Use light weights. The muscles here are small and a heavy weight makes you swing your body instead.
Keep your back flat and your neck in line with your spine. Look at the floor.
Don't lift with your arms bent more than a little, and don't shrug your shoulders up.

steps: Lie on your back across a flat bench, with only your upper back and shoulders on it. Keep your feet flat on the floor and your hips low.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands, cupping the inside of one end, and hold it straight above your chest with your arms almost straight.
Keeping a small bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc back behind your head, as far as you comfortably can. You should feel a stretch through your sides and chest.
Reverse the arc, bringing the dumbbell back over your chest until it's above you again.
watchFor: Hold the dumbbell firmly with both hands. It's above your head and face, so a light weight is the smart choice.
Don't let your lower back arch off the bench or your ribs flare out.
Stop the lowering at the point where you feel a comfortable stretch. Forcing it can strain your shoulders.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the thigh pad so your legs are held snugly under it. Your feet should be flat on the floor.
Reach up and grab the bar with an overhand grip (your palms facing away from you), wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest. Keep your back straight, not rounded.
Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back toward the floor. Focus on squeezing the muscles along your sides.
Pause when the bar reaches your upper chest, then slowly let it rise back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't lean far back and yank the bar down using your body weight. Only your arms and back should move it.
Pull the bar in front of your face, not behind your head. Pulling behind can strain your neck and shoulders.
Control the bar on the way up. Don't let the weight stack slam.

steps: Sit at the machine with your thighs held snugly under the pad and your feet flat on the floor. Attach a narrow handle to the cable if needed.
Grab the handle with your palms facing each other (or facing you, depending on the handle) and your hands close together.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest, keeping your back straight.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and close to your sides.
Pause, then slowly let the handle rise back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Keep your body mostly still. Don't swing back and forth to move the weight.
Keep your shoulders down. Don't shrug them up toward your ears when the bar rises.
Choose a weight you can control the entire way back up.

steps: Sit at the machine with your feet on the footrests and your knees slightly bent. Grab the handle with both hands.
Sit up tall with your chest lifted, your back straight, and your arms straight out in front of you.
Pull the handle toward your lower stomach, driving your elbows straight back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment when your hands reach your stomach.
Slowly let your arms straighten again, letting your shoulders reach forward a little, but keeping your back straight.
watchFor: Keep your back flat and don't lean far back to yank the weight. Only your arms and shoulders should move.
Don't round your lower back as you reach forward.
Let the weight return under control, and don't let the stack crash.

steps: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a straight bar or rope. Stand facing the machine with your feet about hip-width apart.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands about shoulder-width apart, and step back so there's tension in the cable.
Lean forward slightly from your hips with your back flat, and keep your arms almost straight with just a small bend in your elbows.
Pull the bar in a wide arc down to your thighs by squeezing the muscles along your sides. Keep your arms straight.
Pause, then slowly let the bar rise back up to about shoulder height.
watchFor: Keep the small bend in your elbows the same the whole time. Don't turn it into a bending motion.
Don't use your body to push the bar down. Keep your back still.
Use a light weight so that your arms don't take over.

steps: Anchor a long resistance band to something strong and high, like a pull-up bar or a secure door anchor. Make sure it can't slip off.

Kneel or sit facing the anchor and hold the band with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands wider than your shoulders. Your arms should be straight up with a little tension in the band.
Sit up tall and lift your chest.
Pull the band down toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back toward the floor.
Pause, then slowly let your arms rise back up until they're straight.
watchFor: Check the band before each set for cracks or tears, because a snapping band can hit you. Don't use one that looks worn.
Make sure the anchor is secure and can't pop loose.
Control the band on the way up so it doesn't snap your hands back.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the thigh pad so your legs are held snugly. Put your feet flat on the floor.
Reach up and take hold of the handles, following the grip the machine is built for.
Sit tall with your chest lifted and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull the handles down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Pause, then slowly let the handles rise back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Keep your back straight and don't lean far back to help move the weight.
Keep your shoulders down when the arms go up. Don't shrug.
Don't let the weight stack slam when you let go.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the seat and chest pad so you can reach the handles with your arms straight. Put your feet flat on the footrests.
Lean your chest lightly against the pad and sit up tall.
Grab the handles and pull them toward your body by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment when your hands are beside your stomach.
Slowly let your arms straighten again, controlling the handles all the way.
watchFor: Keep your chest against the pad and don't rock your body back and forth.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Don't let the weight stack slam.

steps: Set the weight. On most of these machines a higher number gives you more help, which makes the move easier (check the label on yours). Start with more help than you think you need.
Step onto the platform or kneel on the pad, then reach up and grab the handles.
Hang with your arms straight, your chest lifted, and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down toward your sides until your chin is above the handles.
Pause, then lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Lower yourself under control. Dropping quickly strains your shoulders and elbows.
Don't swing or kick your legs to get up.
As you get stronger, reduce the help a little at a time.

steps: Adjust the machine so the pad sits just below your hips, so you can bend freely at the waist. Your feet should be secured behind the rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold them lightly behind your head.
Bend forward slowly from your hips until you feel a stretch in the back of your thighs. Keep your back straight.
Squeeze your buttocks and lower back to lift your body back up until your body is in one straight line.
Stop when you're in that straight line. Don't lean back past it.
watchFor: Don't arch backward at the top. Lifting past a straight line strains your lower back.
Move slowly and stay in control. Don't swing yourself up.
Start with just your body weight. Only add weight when the movement feels easy and smooth.

steps: Stand under a pull-up bar. Reach up and grab it with an overhand grip (your palms facing away from you), hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Hang with your arms straight. Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you if it helps.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the move, then drive your elbows down toward your sides to lift your body.
Keep pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Don't swing or kick to get up. Use a smooth, controlled movement.
Always lower slowly. Dropping quickly strains your shoulders and elbows.
If you can't do one yet, that's normal. Ask a gym staff member about ways to build up, and hang from the bar to build grip strength.

steps: Stand under a pull-up bar. Reach up and grab it with an underhand grip (palms facing you), hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms straight. Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you if it helps.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then bend your elbows and lift your body, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Keep pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Don't swing or kick. Move smoothly.
Always lower slowly. Dropping quickly strains your elbows and shoulders.
If you can't do one yet, that's normal. Build up gradually, and hang from the bar to build grip and shoulder strength.

steps: Set a bar at about waist height, in a rack or a Smith machine, and make sure it's locked in securely.
Lie on your back under the bar and reach up to grab it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Straighten your body into one long line from your head to your heels, with your heels on the floor and your arms straight.
Tighten your stomach and buttocks. Pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Keep your body in one straight line. Don't let your hips sag.
Make sure the bar is securely locked in place before you hang from it.
To make it easier, bend your knees and put your feet flat on the floor. To make it harder, lower the bar.

steps: Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight and your arms stretched out in front of you.
Keep your neck relaxed, looking at the floor.
At the same time, lift your arms, chest, and legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold that position, squeezing your buttocks and lower back gently.
Lower back to the floor slowly and rest before repeating.
watchFor: Lift only a few inches. Lifting as high as you can strains your lower back.
Don't crane your neck upward. Keep it in line with your spine.
Breathe normally while you hold. If your lower back hurts, lift less.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt, which is a belt with a chain that lets a weight plate hang from your waist. You can also hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Stand under a pull-up bar, reach up, and grab it with an overhand grip (your palms facing away from you), hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Hang with your arms straight and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then drive your elbows down toward your sides to lift your body until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Only add weight once you can do this same movement with just your own body weight, smoothly and with good control. Start with a small weight.
Don't swing. A swinging weight can strain your shoulders and elbows.
Always lower slowly and under control.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt, which is a belt with a chain that lets a weight plate hang from your waist. You can also hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Stand under a pull-up bar, reach up, and grab it with an underhand grip (palms facing you), hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms straight and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then bend your elbows and lift your body, keeping your elbows close to your sides, until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Only add weight once you can do this same movement with just your own body weight, smoothly and with good control. Start with a small weight.
Don't swing or jerk. Move smoothly.
Lower slowly. Dropping fast strains your elbows.
